title: A query given with a folder can't be limited to that folder from the command line, `fff gui`, `fff pick` or /v1/open
problem: `fff gui` documents `fff gui ~/src --query readme` as 'Search for READMEs under ~/src' (nu/fff.nu:148), but the search runs over every search location. `--query` and `/v1/open` carry only a path and a query (src/args.rs:79-85; src/server/mod.rs:622-634; docs/protocol.md:125-129); `open_request` navigates and calls `set_query` without touching the scope (src/finder/mod.rs:805-825); a new window does the same (mod.rs:672-676); the scope starts as `SearchScope::Computer` (mod.rs:549), which sends `scope: None` to the engine (mod.rs:1368-1371). The same holds for `fffinder PATH --query TEXT` and for `fff pick`, `fff insert` (Ctrl+T) and `fff cd`, which pass `--pick <cwd> --query ...` (nu/fff.nu:132-137): the chooser opens at the current folder but its first search is the whole computer, and for a folder outside the search locations it finds nothing there at all. By contrast `/v1/find` and `fff find` do take a scope (src/server/mod.rs:373-381, 409; nu/fff.nu:168-169), and the window has the 'Search Only in' button, so this is the one surface with no way to ask.
proposal: Add an explicit option rather than changing defaults. src/args.rs: `--here` ('With --query, search only inside the folder opened'), stored as `Args.search_here`. src/lib.rs: pass it through `open_window`/`Workspace::new`/`Finder::new` (an extra bool beside `query`) and through `client::forward_open`, which adds a `scope` field set to `folder` to the body. src/server/mod.rs `open()`: read `scope` (`folder` or `computer`, 400 otherwise) into a new `in_folder` field of `UiRequest::Open`. src/finder/mod.rs: `open_request(path, query, in_folder, ..)` and `Finder::new` set `self.scope = SearchScope::Folder` before `set_query` when asked and the location is a folder. nu/fff.nu: `fff gui --here` and `fff pick --here` pass the flag (so a Ctrl+T binding can be made local), and the example becomes `fff gui ~/src --query readme --here`. Update USAGE, docs/protocol.md and the manual's command tables.
original_test_plan: src/args.rs unit test: `--query x --here` parses and sets the field. tests/finder.rs, extending `results_sent_from_nushell` (line 301 onward): `open_request(Some(&projects), Some("roadmap"), true, ..)` gives `search_scope() == SearchScope::Folder` and no rows (Roadmap.md is outside Projects), while `false` lists Roadmap.md. A picker test with `Open { picker: .. }` constructing the Finder with a query and `here`. tests/server.rs `window_requests_reach_the_ui_thread` (line 223): POST `/v1/open` with scope `folder` and assert the `UiRequest::Open` carries it; a bad scope returns 400. tests/nu_module.rs: `fff gui --here` reaches the server when `nu` is installed.
original_risks: Several signatures gain a parameter (open_window, Workspace::new, Finder::new, open_request, UiRequest::Open), which touches the test harness in tests/common/mod.rs:200-216. A folder outside the search locations builds a temporary index on first use (expected, as with the scope bar's folder button).

verifier.claim_check:
The behaviour is as described, with two nuances the candidate misses.

- `--query` carries only text (src/args.rs:79-85; `Args` at 11-25 has no scope field). A second launch forwards only path and query (src/lib.rs:53-59; `forward_open` builds `{"path","query"}` at src/server/client.rs:140-149). `/v1/open` reads only those two (src/server/mod.rs:622-634, `UiRequest::Open` at 38-42), and src/lib.rs:261-278 passes them to `Finder::open_request` or `open_window`.
- `open_request` (src/finder/mod.rs:805-825) navigates and calls `set_query`; it never touches `self.scope`. A new window starts with `scope: SearchScope::Computer` (mod.rs:549) and runs the query at 672-676. `Computer` becomes `scope: None` (mod.rs:1368-1371), and the engine then searches only the search roots (crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:476-479), so a folder outside them is never searched.
- No other handler sets the scope at startup. The only writers are `set_scope` (mod.rs:1461, called from src/finder/bars.rs:81,93 and src/finder/toolbar.rs:435) and `open_smart_folder` (src/finder/filter.rs:219-225). There is no default-scope setting in crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs. `--pick` adds nothing: it builds its own engine over the search roots (src/lib.rs:83-92).
- nu/fff.nu:148 does promise "Search for READMEs under ~/src" for `fff gui ~/src --query readme`, and `help fff gui` prints it (checked with nu 0.116). The example dates from the commit that added `fff gui` (ae057aa) and was never true.
- The current behaviour is not documented as intended. docs/manual.md:60, 75, 1138 and docs/protocol.md:125-129 only say a search starts; manual.md:184 and 326 give the toolbar button as the way to scope. CHANGELOG.md has nothing on it.
- No test pins the scope of a `--query` search. tests/finder.rs:301-308 checks folder, query and location only; tests/controls.rs:329-358 pins the button.

Nuances:
1. On a hand-off the scope is whatever the front tab's Search Only in button was left at, so "every search location" is the default, not a constant.
2. The Ctrl+T and Alt+C bindings run `fff insert` and `fff cd` with no query (nu/fff.nu:390, 397), so there is no "first search" there. What is true is that anything typed in the chooser searches every location.
verifier.implementation_notes:
Keep it opt-in, as proposed, but correct four things.

**1. `--here` must work without `--query`.**
- Define it as "start with Search Only in this folder on", not "With --query, ...".
- The key bindings pass no query, so the proposed wording would do nothing for Ctrl+T.

**2. Don't thread a bool through `open_window`, `Workspace::new` and `Finder::new`.**
- That design also has to edit examples/drive.rs:42, examples/screenshot.rs:169, src/finder/tab_bar.rs:134, tests/settings_file.rs:211 and tests/common/mod.rs:202/216. The candidate lists none of them, and CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings`.
- Instead add next to `set_scope` (src/finder/mod.rs:1461): `pub fn search_here(&mut self, cx)`, which calls `self.set_scope(SearchScope::Folder, cx)` only when `self.current_folder().is_some()`.
- `open_request(path, query, here, window, cx)`: call `if here { self.search_here(cx) }` after the navigation block and before the query block.
  - After, so the scope is the folder just opened.
  - Before, because `set_query` returns early when the text is unchanged (mod.rs:1325) and `set_scope` is then what re-runs the search.
- New windows: in src/lib.rs `run()` (line 148) and the `None` arm of `handle_request` (273), keep the `open_window` call and add `if here && let Some((_, finder)) = opened { finder.update(cx, |f, cx| f.search_here(cx)) }`.
- This is safe: `run_search` bumps `search_gen` and replaces `search_task` (mod.rs:1364-1390), and a dropped gpui Task is cancelled, so the unscoped search `Finder::new` queued never lands. examples/screenshot.rs:195-200 already does the same sequence.
- When `here` is false, leave the scope alone, so today's behaviour is unchanged.

**3. Wire format: a boolean, not `scope: folder|computer`.**
- `scope` is an absolute path in `/v1/find` and `/v1/search` (src/server/mod.rs:373-381).
- A `computer` value mapped to `false` would not switch a window whose button is on.
- Use `UiRequest::Open { path, query, in_folder: bool, reply }`.
- `open()` reads optional `in_folder`: absent or null is false; a non-boolean returns `Failure::bad("in_folder must be true or false")`.
- `client::forward_open(path, query, here)` adds `"in_folder": true` only when set.

**4. Nushell: `fff pick --here` alone does not make Ctrl+T local.**
- Add `--here` to `fff pick` (append `[--here]`) and `fff gui`.
- Pass it through `fff insert`, `fff cd` and `fff edit` as `fff pick --here=$here ...$query`. I checked that this parses and forwards on nu 0.116, the version CI pins.
- Add `fff keybindings --here`, which binds `fff insert --here` and `fff cd --here`.
- The example at nu/fff.nu:148 becomes `fff gui ~/src --query readme --here`.

**Remaining edits**
- src/args.rs: `pub here: bool`, the `"--here"` arm, a USAGE line, and the module comment. The exhaustive `Args { .. }` literal in `parses_pick_contract` (126-135) needs the new field.
- src/main.rs needs no change: `detach` forwards every argument except `--detach` (line 34).
- src/lib.rs:57 passes `args.here` to `forward_open`.
- tests/server.rs:247 destructures `UiRequest::Open { path, query, reply }` exhaustively and must be updated.
- docs/manual.md: options block 53-70, its bullets and the hand-off sentence at 75, line 326, line 730, and the table at 1137-1143. Say that it stays on in that window until the button is clicked.
- docs/protocol.md:125-129 and a CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` Added entry.

Optional, same helper: `Workspace::move_tab_to_new_window` (src/workspace.rs:245-253) drops the tab's scope today.

All of this runs on Linux.

- `--here` parses alone, with `--pick`, and with `--query`.
- Update the struct literal in `parses_pick_contract`.

**tests/finder.rs** (harness in tests/common/mod.rs: `Fixture::new`, `Ui::open`, `ui.update`, `ui.read`, `ui.names()`, `ui.exists`)
- Add `false` to the two existing calls at 303 and 312.
- New test, using "budget" rather than the candidate's "roadmap", because tests/controls.rs:339-345 already pins that pair:
  - `open_request(Some(&projects), Some("budget"), false, ..)` gives `search_scope() == Computer` and `names() == ["Budget.csv"]`.
  - The same with `true` gives `Folder`, `names().is_empty()` and `ui.exists("scope-folder")`.
  - `open_request(Some(&projects), Some("atlas"), true, ..)` contains "Project Atlas.txt".
- Unchanged-query case: in a fresh window at Projects searching "budget" unscoped, `open_request(None, Some("budget"), true, ..)` empties the rows.
- Non-folder case: after `f.navigate(Location::Recents, ..)`, `open_request(None, None, true, ..)` leaves `Computer`.
- New-window path, opened the way tests/settings_file.rs:207-215 opens extra windows:
  - `ui.cx.update(|cx| ..)` calls `fffinder::open_window(Location::Folder(projects), Some("budget".into()), None, cx)` and then `finder.update(cx, |f, cx| f.search_here(cx))`.
  - After `ui.settle()`, `finder.read_with(ui.cx, ..)` shows scope `Folder` and `rows_for_test().is_empty()`.
  - This proves the constructor's unscoped search does not land.
- Chooser: `Ui::open_with(cx, &fx.dir, Open { picker: Some(PickerOptions { multiple: false }), ..Default::default() })`, `ui.go_to(&projects)`, `ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.search_here(cx))`, `ui.click("search")`, `ui.type_text("budget")`, then `names().is_empty()`.
- Don't add a UI test for a folder outside the search roots: the temporary index scans on real threads and the harness clock is fake.

**tests/server.rs `window_requests_reach_the_ui_thread` (223)**
- The `seen` vector is never asserted (`let _ = ui;` at 289), so have the stand-in echo the flag in its reply, for example `Err(format!("no such folder, in_folder={in_folder}"))`.
- Assert `in_folder=true` for `{"query":"x","in_folder":true}` and `in_folder=false` when the field is absent.
- Assert a 400 containing "in_folder must be true or false" for `"in_folder": "yes"`.

**tests/nu_module.rs** (`#[cfg(unix)]`, skipped without nu)
- Do not run the real binary: `fff gui` would start a GUI if the hand-off failed, and it reads the real settings folder.
- Point `$env.FFFINDER_BIN` at a stub shell script that writes its arguments to a file and prints `[]`.
- Assert `fff gui <dir> --query readme --here` records `--detach <dir> --query readme --here`.
- Assert `fff pick --here budget` and `fff cd --here x` record `--here`.
- Assert `fff keybindings --here` sets the `fff_insert` binding's cmd to `fff insert --here`.
- I ran this stub approach against the current module with nu 0.116 and it records the arguments as expected.
verifier.risks:
- The scope is sticky. After `--here` reaches a running window, that tab keeps Search Only in on, so a later `--query` without `--here` is still scoped until the button is clicked. The button already behaves this way; the manual must say so.
- In a chooser inside a search location, `--here` narrows results but is no faster. Each `--pick` process indexes every search root itself (src/lib.rs:83-92), and a scoped search waits for the covering root's scan.
- A folder outside the search locations gets a watched temporary index, and only three are kept (engine.rs:26). This matches the button.
- Scoped searches don't list apps (`wants_apps` needs no scope, engine.rs:1488). This also matches the button.
- Version skew: an older fffinder that is still running ignores `in_folder` and searches unscoped. An older binary rejects `--here` as an unknown option.
- `--here` with a PATH that doesn't exist scopes to whatever folder the window falls back to.
- Merge care: the worktrees /home/user/fffinder-lane-b and /home/user/fffinder-lane-c have uncommitted edits in src/finder/mod.rs, tests/finder.rs and docs/manual.md. The hunks differ, and the corrected plan stays out of tests/common/mod.rs, which lane-c also edits.
- The value rating of 3 depends on corrections 1 and 4 (works without `--query`, and the pass-through to `fff insert`, `fff cd` and `fff keybindings`). Without them the flag only serves `fff gui`, and it is closer to a 2.
